# Overview {.unnumbered}

Most published sequencing papers deposit their raw reads in a public
archive. Re-using them is one of the cheapest experiments in biology: a
control for your own data, a new question asked of an old dataset, or a way
to learn a pipeline. Getting the files out, though, is less obvious than it
should be. This guide explains, from the beginning, how to go from "the
paper says the data are in GEO" to a folder of `.fastq.gz` files ready for
a pipeline such as [bagPipes](https://github.com/PhanstielLab/bagPipes).

It's written for wet-lab scientists who are new to the command line. If
terms like *FASTQ*, *gzip* or *SLURM* are unfamiliar, the first chapters of
[omics-walkthru](https://jpflores-13.github.io/omics-walkthru) explain them.

## The short version

```bash
module load sratoolkit                         # or install it (see Setup)
prefetch SRR1039508 --max-size u               # 1. download the .sra file
vdb-validate SRR1039508                        # 2. check it
fasterq-dump SRR1039508 --threads 6 --temp /path/to/scratch   # 3. convert to FASTQ
pigz -p 6 SRR1039508*.fastq                    # 4. compress (gzip works too)
```

That gives `SRR1039508_1.fastq.gz` and `SRR1039508_2.fastq.gz`. Everything
else in this guide explains each of those lines, how to find the accession,
how to do it for 50 samples at once on Longleaf, and how to check and
organise what you got.

## The whole path

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  P["Paper<br/>'data in GEO GSE52778'"] --> G["GEO series<br/>GSE → GSM samples"]
  G --> S["SRA Run Selector<br/>GSM → SRR runs<br/>+ metadata table"]
  S --> L["Accession list<br/>SRR_Acc_List.txt"]
  L --> PF["prefetch<br/>.sra files"]
  PF --> V["vdb-validate"]
  V --> FQ["fasterq-dump<br/>FASTQ"]
  FQ --> Z["compress<br/>.fastq.gz"]
  Z --> M["merge runs per sample,<br/>rename, samplesheet"]
  M --> B["pipeline<br/>(bagPipes)"]
  S -.-> E["ENA: same data<br/>as ready-made .fastq.gz"]
  E -.-> M
```

## How this guide is organised

| Part | Chapters | Read it when |
|---|---|---|
| Concepts | [The databases](chapters/databases.qmd), [Accessions](chapters/accessions.qmd), [Finding the data](chapters/finding-data.qmd) | You have a paper and want to know what to download |
| Downloading | [Setup](chapters/setup.qmd), [prefetch](chapters/prefetch.qmd), [fasterq-dump](chapters/fasterq-dump.qmd), [At scale on Longleaf](chapters/at-scale.qmd) | You're ready to download |
| After the download | [Verify and organise](chapters/verify-organise.qmd), [Worked example](chapters/worked-example.qmd) | You have FASTQs and want to run a pipeline |
| Appendices | [ENA](chapters/ena.qmd), [Special cases](chapters/special-cases.qmd), [Troubleshooting](chapters/troubleshooting.qmd), [Cheat sheet](chapters/cheatsheet.qmd) | Something is unusual, or you just need the commands |

The repository's `scripts/` folder has ready-to-use scripts for each step:

| Script | Does |
|---|---|
| [`scripts/download_sra.sh`](https://github.com/jpflores-13/download-public-data/blob/main/scripts/download_sra.sh) | SLURM array job: prefetch → validate → fasterq-dump → compress, one run per task |
| [`scripts/merge_runs.sh`](https://github.com/jpflores-13/download-public-data/blob/main/scripts/merge_runs.sh) | Combine runs belonging to the same sample and rename to `<sample>_R1_001.fastq.gz` |
| [`scripts/ena_download.sh`](https://github.com/jpflores-13/download-public-data/blob/main/scripts/ena_download.sh) | Download ready-made `.fastq.gz` from ENA and check MD5s |

::: {.callout-note}
## Running example

Throughout, we use the **airway** dataset (GEO
[GSE52778](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE52778); Himes
*et al.*, *PLoS One* 2014): RNA-seq of human airway smooth muscle cells from
four donors, untreated or treated with dexamethasone. It's paired-end, about
20–40 million read pairs per run, and widely used for teaching (it is the
Bioconductor `airway` package). Files for it are in `examples/`.
:::
